title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren't broadcasting their location | New Scientist
description: Researchers have found that seabirds equipped with audio recorders and GPS trackers can detect ships, offering a way to monitor fishing vessels that are operating illegally
author: Shosha Adie

title: AI's stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it | New Scientist
description: The biggest problem in maths has been cracked by AI, but it remains impossible to predict how its capabilities will advance in other fields
author: New Scientist

title: Basic income trial in Peru aims to prove rainforest protection merits | New Scientist
description: A trial starting in 2027 will see Indigenous people in the Amazon given no-strings cash payments in the hopes of reducing deforestation
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: OpenAI discovers efficiency limit for multiplying large sets of numbers | New Scientist
description: Matrix multiplication is a problem intrinsic in almost all software, and now AI has revealed how efficiently algorithms can theoretically do it - but achieving this ideal is another matter
author: Matthew Sparkes

title: An atom-sized black hole could force an entire star to explode | New Scientist
description: The early universe may have produced minuscule black holes, and if they are still around today they could devour stars from the inside or blow them up entirely
author: Leah Crane

title: AI is forcing researchers to confront the possibility of artificial minds | New Scientist
description: Neuroscientists and philosophers met at a conference to discuss ‘exotic, mind-like entities’ – and how chatbots might be moulding our own minds
author: Jo Marchant
